companyDescription: Space data & analytics · 100+ nanosatellite constellation for weather (GNSS-RO), maritime/aviation tracking, and RF geolocation · $65M+ in fresh NOAA/EUMETSAT bookings since August · Diehl Defence missile-tracking MOU still the moonshot lever
priceNote: Live $9.00 (-0.7%) at Oct 26, 2026 open — down ~21% from $11.34 at the Sep 29 report; 52-week range $6.60-$25.93. Market cap ~$352M. Since the Sep 29 reports, this board's small caps fell 21-41% after the Sep 16 hike and the hot Sep CPI (Oct 14). This is a sector/size selloff that SPY-based regime notes don't capture, so drawdowns here say as much about the tape as the thesis.
summary: REFRESH (prior report Sep 29, 2026): SPIR fell ~21% despite a $33.2M NOAA award and its first Colorado-built satellites. Q3 earnings (~Nov 11, est.) are now the dated catalyst, and the read is bookings conversion vs. the Q2 gross-margin hit (34%, WildFireSat cancellation). ⚠️ Tier-2 note: partnership_win is the measured Tier-2 LAGGARD in turbo feedback (medianExcessVsBenchPct -3.8pp vs +2.0pp overall, n=16; 3/16 windows had SPY down >2%), and it is independently the laggard in the core lane too (-1.6 vs +1.4, n=12). That calls for visibly higher conviction to hold a slot, and the Diehl MOU is still non-binding, so sizing drops to the 2% floor. Base cut from +70% to +45% (above the lane's realized 30d P90 of +25.9%; written-Base bias +72.7pp). It assumes 3-6 months of bookings converting to revenue. แนะนำ 2% ของ portfolio เท่านั้น — ถ้า thesis fail ลงได้ 35-50%.

catalysts.name: Q3 2026 earnings — bookings vs. margin
catalysts.description: First print since the $33.2M NOAA weather-data award and the first Colorado-built satellites. The read is whether bookings convert while gross margin recovers from the Q2 WildFireSat hit. Date estimated (sources show Nov 2 to Nov 11).

catalysts.name: Diehl Defence missile-tracking MOU
catalysts.description: Still a non-binding MOU — the moonshot lever if it converts to a funded program.

risks: Gross margin slipped to 34% in Q2 on the WildFireSat contract cancellation; Q3 needs to show recovery.

partnership_win is the measured Tier-2 LAGGARD in turbo feedback (medianExcessVsBenchPct -3.8pp vs +2.0pp overall, n=16; 3/16 windows had SPY down >2%), and it is independently the laggard in the core lane too (-1.6 vs +1.4, n=12). Contract headlines have not reliably converted into sustained re-rates lane-wide.
The Diehl Defence relationship is still a non-binding MOU with no confirmed progress. The moonshot lever is undated.
TTM revenue is down ~33% (post-maritime divestiture), and the business depends on lumpy government renewals and appropriations.
52-week range $6.60-$25.93: this stock has already round-tripped a huge move once this cycle.

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed funds at 3.75-4.00% after the surprise Sep 16, 2026 hike (first since 2023). The Oct 27-28 FOMC is priced ~93% hold / ~7% +25bp as of Oct 25 — but hike odds briefly spiked to ~44% after the hot Sep CPI print on Oct 14, so the path stays two-sided.
macroRisk.inflationNote: September CPI +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y headline; core +0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y — both above consensus. Headline re-acceleration keeps a further 2026 hike live.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Government-contract space-data company. Rates affect the small-cap multiple more than the business, which depends on appropriations.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — Oct 28 hold is priced (~93%), but hot CPI keeps a further 2026 hike live. Small, cash-burning names have already absorbed most of this tape's damage, so a hold is mildly supportive and a surprise hike is the main macro tail.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Falling, not running: SPIR is ~21% below the Sep 29 report price despite the NOAA award, consistent with the partnership_win lane pattern of contract headlines not sticking.

postWin.note: Redwire (RDW) rallied roughly 220% on Golden Dome missile-defense contract momentum (SHIELD IDIQ award, Feb 2026) — the closest same-theme comparable for what a Diehl Defence contract conversion could do to SPIR. Per this run's tier2 feedback, partnership_win is a lane-wide laggard (-3.8pp vs +2.0pp overall, n=16), so this needs to be a real conversion, not just incremental bookings, to move the needle.

postLose.note: SPIR's own Q2 2026 print is now the most relevant precedent — a genuinely strong bookings quarter ($65M+ in new contracts) still produced a -17.8% stock decline over six weeks on the WildFireSat margin miss, showing this stock can fall hard even on net-positive news.

spotSizing.reason: 2% max. partnership_win is the measured Tier-2 LAGGARD in turbo feedback (medianExcessVsBenchPct -3.8pp vs +2.0pp overall, n=16; 3/16 windows had SPY down >2%), and it is independently the laggard in the core lane too (-1.6 vs +1.4, n=12). That calls for visibly higher conviction, and a non-binding MOU doesn't provide it, so sizing sits at the floor.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Wider than the partnership_win medianMAE (-25.9%, n=16). A break of the 52-week low before Q3 means the bookings story isn't being believed.

stopPostCatalyst.note: If Q3 shows margin still falling or bookings not converting, exit — the laggard pattern says not to wait for the MOU.
